title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 12 of the notes on the structure at infinity of M_{g,nu}, a digression on 'deployments' of normal-crossings divisors. The previous page stated a general van Kampen theorem: the punctured-neighbourhood topos V*_{Sigma,X} is the 2-colimit of a semi-simplicial system of topoi (groupoids of analytic multiplicities) indexed by the intersection types D_{d_0..d_r}. Here Grothendieck checks the formalism against the simplest case.

The case: X = D_0 is a smooth connected curve (compact, say). Theta is a reduced smooth divisor, i.e. a finite set of points. X* = X \ Theta. V_{Theta,X} is a tubular neighbourhood of Theta, a disjoint union of discs. V*_{Theta,X} is that neighbourhood with Theta removed, a disjoint union of punctured discs.

He remarks that here the heavy formalism is overkill. The 'van Kampen theorem' becomes almost tautological and purely topological: X is obtained by gluing X* to the discs along the punctured discs, one for each point of Theta.

This gives a description of pi_1(X) (explicitly 'and not pi_1(X*)') as an amalgamated sum of groupoids, with base points taken on Theta (or the punctured discs):
  pi_1(X) = pi_1(X*) *_{pi_1(V*_{Theta,X})} pi_1(V_{Theta,X}).
- pi_1(V*) is a groupoid with one object per point of Theta, each with automorphism group Z.
- pi_1(V_{Theta,X}) is the discrete groupoid with Theta as set of vertices (he underlines and annotates this).

So the pushout kills the loops around the punctures. In his simplicial notation this is the span Pi~_{1,0} -> Pi~_0 and Pi~_{1,0} -> (Pi_{1,0}, discrete), labelled formula (254).

The next page generalises the question. For admissible parts Sigma ⊂ Sigma', he wants to express pi_1 Sigma, pi_1(Sigma' \ Sigma), pi_1 V*_{Sigma,X} and pi_1 V*_{Sigma',Sigma,X*} in terms of the pi~_{Delta_r} and pi_{Delta_r}. He also wants to add the missing structure, namely traces V_{Sigma',Sigma''} ∩ Sigma_1. This page thus marks the realisation that the formalism of the previous section yields the punctured neighbourhood / complement side, but must be enriched to recover the fundamental groupoids of closed unions of strata and of their complements.
errors: No mathematical error. The pushout description of pi_1(X) via groupoid van Kampen is correct. It needs base points on the punctured discs (or one base point per point of Theta), which the groupoid formulation handles.

ideas.what: pi_1 of a curve as amalgamated sum of groupoids: pi_1(X*) and the discrete groupoid on Theta, over the groupoid of punctured discs. Filling punctures kills the boundary loops.
ideas.modern_name: van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids with several base points
ideas.where_published: Groupoid-style van Kampen appears in SGA1 exp. IX (descent for pi_1) in the étale setting.

ideas.what: Using the tubular neighbourhood minus the divisor (system of punctured neighbourhoods indexed by strata of a normal-crossings divisor) to dévisser homotopy types at infinity.
ideas.modern_name: link / boundary of a tubular neighbourhood; Kato–Nakayama log space or real oriented blow-up; homotopy-colimit decomposition along a stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points), Kato–Nakayama (1999), stratified homotopy theory (Quinn, Lurie)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of the 'structure at infinity' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without this formalism.

missed.claim: Grothendieck recognises that his van Kampen formalism for the punctured neighbourhood system must be enriched to recover pi_1 of closed unions of strata and of their complements from the semi-simplicial data pi~_{Delta_r}, pi_{Delta_r}. He starts doing this on the next page. This is a step in his programme of describing pi_1 of M_{g,nu} via boundary strata, largely superseded by later stratified homotopy theory and log-geometry approaches.
missed.quote: donne une description de pi_1(X) (et non pi_1(X*)) comme somme amalgamée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It documents his groupoid-theoretic approach to the boundary of moduli stacks. The mathematics on this page itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a sanity check of a general formalism against the trivial curve case, reproducing the standard groupoid van Kampen pushout. It is historically interesting as part of the M_{g,nu} 'structure at infinity' programme, but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'la "th. de recollement"' should likely read 'le "Th. de van Kampen"', referring back to the previous page.
'se ramène [?] en principe [?] topologique' likely reads 'est un peu tautologique', followed by 'revient à dire que...'.
'Il y a équivalence [?] bien entendu' is more likely 'Il y a cependant ici bien entendu...'.
Struck words after 'pi_1(X*' include a crossed-out Theta, giving 'X* = X \ Theta' as written under it.
'Leur dévissage en types d'intersection' is uncertain; the final word looks more like 'élémentaires', with an insertion mark after 'types'.
The marginal note under pi_1 V_{Theta,X} reads 'groupoïde discret défini par Theta comme ens. de sommets'.
